extraction.tier_rationale: Standard reference-adult LA disposition value (Tier-C). Ropivacaine (S-enantiomer) has lower lipid solubility and slightly higher clearance than racemic bupivacaine, and is markedly less cardiotoxic (the v0.6 LA2 agent-choice argument).

extraction.tier_rationale: Site-absorption rank order robust; absolute ka Tier-C, applied site-wise.

toxicity_thresholds.method_caveat: Volunteer slow i.v. infusion (Knudsen 1997): CNS symptoms at higher total plasma than bupivacaine (~3.4 ug/mL mean) — ropivacaine is less potent and less toxic. Speed of rise and acidosis lower the threshold; a rapid intravascular injection is not this slow-infusion number.
toxicity_thresholds.saturation_caveat: Ropivacaine binding is SATURABLE: this total-basis range under-predicts free-drug risk at high total concentration (the free fraction rises non-linearly; non-linear model is v0.6 LA3).

toxicity_thresholds.method_caveat: Ropivacaine's cardiovascular margin OVER its CNS-warning range is the WIDEST of the long-acting amides (less avid cardiac Na-channel binding; the S-enantiomer and reduced lipophilicity) — wider than levobupivacaine's, much wider than racemic bupivacaine's. The agent-choice safety differentiation (v0.6 LA2). Magnitude Tier-C and method-dependent; the load-bearing fact is the margin ORDER (bupivacaine < levobupivacaine < ropivacaine), not a precise number.
toxicity_thresholds.saturation_caveat: Saturable binding: this total-basis cardiovascular range under-predicts free-drug risk at high total concentration (v0.6 LA3).

extraction.tier_rationale: CVS thresholds are wide, method-dependent and ethically un-doseable in volunteers; Tier-C. The clinically load-bearing claim is the WIDER ropivacaine CNS-to-CVS margin vs bupivacaine.
extraction.source_locator: Knudsen 1997; Scott 1989 (acute toxicity, ropivacaine vs bupivacaine)

extraction.tier_rationale: v0.6 LA0: systemic disposition + site absorption only — no toxicity thresholds (LA1). Disposition + ka Tier-C; the site rank is the robust claim.

source_review.notes: CITATION DISCREPANCY (values not changed): ropivacaine is cited to Tucker & Mather 1979, but ropivacaine had no human PK until the late 1980s. The curated Vss 59 L matches EXACTLY the first human study, Lee et al. 1989 (PMID 2589653; GT Tucker is a co-author, which likely explains the citation drift). HUMAN ACTION: re-cite to Lee 1989 and/or the FDA Naropin label. Note blood-based (Lee, Vss 59 L, CL 0.72) vs plasma-based (FDA, Vdss 41 L, CL 0.39) reference frames differ; the curated set mixes the blood Vss with a plasma-leaning CL.

notes: Systemic concentration only. The S-enantiomer's wider cardiovascular margin vs bupivacaine at similar CNS potency is the v0.6 LA2 educational comparison.
